title: Instantaneous velocity at t=2s
description: Essential: Correctly reads or calculates the instantaneous velocity at the end of the 2nd second as 3 m/s.

title: Average acceleration (first 3s)
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the average acceleration for the first 3 seconds using a = (v_f - v_i)/Δt, yielding approximately 1.67 m/s².

title: Average acceleration (last 2s)
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the average acceleration for the last 2 seconds using a = (v_f - v_i)/Δt, yielding -2.5 m/s² (magnitude 2.5 m/s²).

title: Average velocity (4th second)
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the average velocity during the 4th second using v_avg = Δx/Δt, yielding 4 m/s.

title: Correct velocity identification
description: Important: Identifies the correct initial and final velocities for each time interval from the provided data.

title: Proper acceleration sign
description: Important: Recognizes that the acceleration during the last 2 seconds is negative (deceleration) but reports its magnitude correctly.

title: Position difference method
description: Optional: Uses the change in position over the 4th second (from t=3s to t=4s) to compute average velocity, not just an average of speeds.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: Includes correct units (m/s, m/s²) with all numerical answers.

title: Sign error in acceleration
description: Pitfall: Reports a positive value for the acceleration during the last 2 seconds without indicating it's a magnitude or confuses acceleration with deceleration sign.

title: Wrong time interval
description: Pitfall: Uses incorrect time intervals (e.g., 0-2s for first acceleration, 6-8s as 3s interval) or misidentifies the 4th second.
